rows.text: loads qword `+0` and qword `+0x10` of `rcx`, calls `00628570(qword +0, 0, 1)` and `006215A0(qword +0, 1, qword +0x10, qword +0x10 + 0x40)` with stack arguments 0, 4 and 0, then tail-jumps `00628570(qword +0, 1, 1)`
dereferences the pointers at `rdx` and `rcx` and sets `al` to 1 when the float `+0x34` of the `rdx` object is below, equal to or unordered with the float `+0x34` of the `rcx` object, else 0

scans the qword vector from `+0` to `+8` of `rcx` for `rdx`; when found, calls `001F6E60(rdx)` and `001BCE30(rcx+0x20, &that result)`, allocates `0x20` bytes through slot `+0x10` of the object at `+0x10` of the returned node, writes the pair {`rdx`, 3} at the new block's `+0x10` and links the block before that node, then moves the vector's last qword into the found slot and subtracts 8 from qword `+8`; on every path tail-jumps `0016D6A0(1 when the vector's count changed else 0, "Can't find character object when try to remove it!" (`008F9520`))`

takes the floats `+0x30`, `+0x34` and `+0x38` of `rdx` (zeros when `rdx` is null) and, when any differs from (or is unordered with) the floats `+0x244`, `+0x248`, `+0x24C` of `rcx`, stores them there and byte 1 at `+0x240`; then calls `001EF060(element, rdx)` for each qword from `+0x18` up to `+0x20` of `rcx` (none when `+0x18` is above `+0x20`)

walks 0x18-byte elements from `rcx` up to `rdx` with a parallel 0x18-byte destination from `r8`, and for each non-null destination stores `009010B8` at its `+0`, copies the source's qword `+8` and byte `+0x10` to the same offsets, then stores `00903940` at `+0`; returns the destination pointer past the last element (`r8` unchanged when `rcx` equals `rdx`)
returns qword `+0x2A0` of the object at qword `+0x488` of `rcx`

notes: Doubts: 001BD840 - the 16-byte pair copy at 001BD8CF-001BD8D4 is skipped when the allocated pointer plus 0x10 is zero, while the list link at 001BD8D7-001BD8EC uses the block on every found path; the row folds that guard into 'writes'. The loop index and count are 32-bit (edi, ebx, unsigned jb). 001AD470 sets only al (the rest of rax holds the pointer loaded at entry). 001F4C00's 009010B8 and 00903940 are lea-resolved .rdata addresses (stored as the element's first qword, so likely vtables), not jump tables.
